answer: Clique-cost ledger: each agent pays a fee proportional to the number of distinct agents its actions touch within a window. Coordination across many fresh identities triggers rising fees because each new counterpart inflates the payer's contact count. Identities route payments through a shared vault, so colluding clusters pay repeatedly. A karst of dormant sockpuppets still costs their operator to activate. Under gale-like burst registration, the fee multiplier compounds, making N-identity coordination cost roughly N² while honest pairwise trades stay cheap.
